assessment.snapshot: Lane gets on base by drawing walks, runs the bases well and drives in runs, while handling every defensive chance cleanly. Catching is the main area to polish, especially blocking pitches, and the bat needs more hard contact for extra bases.

strengths.title: Plate Discipline
strengths.detail: Draws walks at a high rate, so on-base percentage is well above batting average. Strikeouts stay at a manageable level for this age.

strengths.title: Baserunning
strengths.detail: Steals bases successfully every time he tries, showing good instincts and the ability to take the extra base.

strengths.title: Run Production
strengths.detail: Drives in a lot of runs for the number of plate appearances, so he is coming through with runners on.

strengths.title: Fielding
strengths.detail: Handles every chance cleanly, with no errors across a good number of chances.

assessment.battingReason: Walks often, reaches base at a high rate and steals bases successfully. Singles-only contact fits a lead-off or second spot, though the sample is small.
assessment.confidenceReason: Only 19 plate appearances and under 17 innings caught, so rates like AVG, BB% and K% can swing a lot. No coach ratings were provided to compare, and fielding is not split by position.

practice.drills: Target-based bullpens with a catcher's mitt or strike-zone net, 'ladder' drills that track strikes out of 10 pitches, short side sessions for all seven pitchers, first-pitch strike challenges, and a basic repeatable-delivery routine.

Blocking drills with balls in the dirt, receiving and framing work, quick transfer and pop-time drills from the crouch, and pitcher-catcher work on holding runners and varying looks. Cross-train a third catcher, such as a strong-armed infielder like Eli or Casey.

practice.focus: Contact hitting for bottom of the order
practice.drills: Tee work and soft toss focused on bat-to-ball contact, front toss with a short compact swing, two-strike approach drills, and tracking drills to cut down swinging strikeouts for Alex and Drew.

Ground ball reps with a focus on glove position and fielding through the ball, throwing accuracy to a target, and fly ball drills with drop-step and route practice for players with lower glove ratings.

Hitters who walk often can work on attacking pitches in the zone with batting practice rounds that reward line drives and gap hits, plus a count-based approach that stays selective but aggressive on good pitches.

team.summary: This team has an excellent offense built on patience, speed and clean baserunning, and its fielding is steady. The priorities are pitching control and catcher depth and run prevention, since walks and free stolen bases are giving back much of what the lineup earns. Smaller goals are better contact from the bottom of the order and building extra-base power.
defensiveConcerns: Only two players can catch, and opponents are running on them almost freely
Pitching staff has little control, even with seven pitchers available
Drew and Indy have limited defensive range, with few safe positions
Primary catcher Hayden also pitches, which could be a workload concern

weaknesses.title: Pitching Control
weaknesses.detail: Pitching is the biggest gap. The staff issues too many walks and allows far too many baserunners. Strikeout stuff exists (Casey, Eli, Hayden), but strikes are not being thrown consistently. Every pitcher needs to work on the strike zone.

weaknesses.title: Catcher Depth and Run Prevention
weaknesses.detail: Only two players can catch, and opponents run freely, with almost no runners thrown out. Passed balls are also a problem for the primary catcher, so blocking and receiving need work. Any injury or fatigue at catcher would leave a real hole.

weaknesses.title: Strikeouts for Bottom of the Order
weaknesses.detail: Contact is a clear issue for a few hitters. Alex and Drew strike out often and have not recorded a hit, relying on walks to reach base.

weaknesses.title: Defensive Weak Spots
weaknesses.detail: Some players have low glove and arm ratings, which limits where they can be placed safely. Drew and Indy are the clearest examples, with Jules's arm also a concern.

weaknesses.title: Extra-Base Power
weaknesses.detail: Many hitters are slap or walk-first types without extra-base hits. Added hard contact would turn more baserunners into runs.

strengths.title: On-Base Ability
strengths.detail: The lineup gets on base at a very high rate, driven by patience at the plate. Walks are a major part of the offense and keep pressure on opposing pitchers.

strengths.title: Baserunning
strengths.detail: The team steals bases aggressively and has not been caught. Speed and good reads on the bases create extra scoring chances. Many players contribute, with Gray leading the way.

strengths.title: Fielding Consistency
strengths.detail: The team fields the ball cleanly with very few errors. Sure hands in the infield and at catcher keep innings from extending.

strengths.title: Run Production
strengths.detail: Several hitters at the top of the order combine contact with extra-base power and drive in runs. Eli, Finn and Jules are the standouts.

strengths.title: Positional Flexibility
strengths.detail: Most players can handle several infield and outfield spots, which gives the coach many ways to build the defensive alignment. Seven players can pitch.

lineup.battingRationale: The order is sorted by on-base and slugging production from GameChanger, since no coach ratings or notes were provided. Top hitters get the most plate appearances, with speed and OBP at the top and power in the 3-5 spots. Tradeoff: Alex and Drew bat last to favor winning, but they still get regular at-bats for development, and their high walk rates show real patience to build on.
warnings: Lane catches innings 1-4 and Hayden catches innings 5-6. Hayden pitches in innings 3-4 and then catches, which is legal.
Several players are at positions where they are not rated strongest, such as Blake in RF and Indy at 1B, because the rotation and the infield rule require it.
lineup.defenseRationale: Pitching goes to Eli, Hayden and Casey for 2 innings each, using the strongest pitching stats among eligible players. Lane and Hayden split catching, and the best gloves stay at SS and 2B. Sitting is spread so each player sits at most twice, never in consecutive innings. Everyone gets an infield inning by the 4th. The tradeoff is that development rotations put a few players out of their primary positions in some innings.
